issues.legal_issue: Municipal property tax recoverable from a tenant as rent cannot be added to the contractual rent to remove the tenant’s protection from eviction under rent-control law.
material_facts: The tenant’s contractual rent was below the threshold for protection under rent-control law.
After a change in the method of municipal property-tax assessment, the landlord paid property tax for the premises and sought to recover the tenant’s share as rent.
The landlord claimed that adding the recoverable tax to the contractual rent took the premises above the protection threshold and sought possession after the tenant did not pay the tax.
issues.conclusion: The recoverable property tax could not be treated as part of the rent for determining whether the tenant lost protection from eviction. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The rent-control statute is a special enactment governing landlord-tenant matters and, under Section 14, protects tenants from eviction except on specified grounds. Section 3(c) defines the premises excluded by the monthly-rent threshold, while Section 7(2) bars a landlord from recovering building or land tax from a tenant, whether by an increase in rent or otherwise. Section 50 bars civil-court proceedings on matters assigned to the Controller. Although Sections 67(1) and 67(3) of the municipal statute permit recovery of certain property tax from a tenant with the same rights and remedies as for rent, that provision does not override the rent-control statute’s protection against eviction; Section 411 also provides that other laws are not to be disregarded. The Court relied on Life Insurance Corporation of India v. D.J. Bahadur and Sanwarmal Kejriwal v. Viswa Co-operative Housing Society Ltd. for the primacy of a special enactment on its subject, and on St Stephen’s College v. University of Delhi, Gobind Sugar Mills Ltd. v. State of Bihar, and Commercial Tax Officer, Rajasthan v. Binani Cements Limited for principles of harmonious construction and the relationship between general and special laws. Ganga Ram v. Mohd. Usman concerned recovery of enhanced tax, not eviction, and did not decide this issue.

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession of premises from a tenant.
predicates.base_rent_within_tenant_protection: The contractual monthly rent was within the range in which rent-control protection applied.
predicates.landlord_sought_to_add_unpaid_municipal_: The landlord sought to count municipal property tax recoverable from the tenant as rent.
predicates.tax_addition_would_put_monthly_total_abo: Counting the tax together with the contractual rent would put the monthly total above the threshold for rent-control protection.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns premises whose contractual rent is within the protection range and the landlord seeks to count unpaid municipal tax as rent to cross the protection threshold, the tax is excluded from rent for deciding whether the tenant retains that protection.
